This record cannot restore a pre-registration after the fact; it classifies every analysis so a reader can tell confirmatory from exploratory.

analysis_register.analysis: ATTAINABLE-CEILING NORMALISATION of the primary metric. Devised after observing that the raw tier curve conflates model degradation with the falling maximum score a single-label predictor can obtain as annotators disagree. Materially changes the headline RQ1 magnitude claim. POST-HOC and reported as such; the pre-registered raw-scale result is retained alongside it.
Class-composition control: S-unanimous per-class accuracy re-weighted by each contested tier's class mix, to test whether the tier effect is a class-mix effect

corrections_to_the_delivered_report.claim: the any-annotator hit rate 'shows no such reversal' and therefore the non-monotonicity at S-plurality is measurement noise
corrections_to_the_delivered_report.evidence: The report's own Table 2 gives any-hit 84.39 / 80.02 / 72.70 / 79.83 across the four ordered tiers -- the identical dip at S-plurality followed by recovery. The metric shows the same reversal it was cited as not showing.
corrections_to_the_delivered_report.replacement: The non-monotonicity is assessed by the S-plurality - S-no-majority bootstrap gap: -4.63 points, 95% CI [-9.29, +1.87] on the raw scale (not distinguishable from zero), and -17.83 points, 95% CI [-31.25, -2.64] on the ceiling-normalised scale (significantly negative -- a genuine reversal, not noise).

corrections_to_the_delivered_report.claim: the any-annotator hit rate is a fair cross-tier comparator
corrections_to_the_delivered_report.evidence: The size of the accepted label set differs by tier: mean distinct annotator labels per image is 1.00 (S-unanimous), 2.00 (S-majority), 3.00 (S-plurality), 2.20 (S-no-majority). A prediction has up to three times as many ways to score a hit on S-plurality as on S-unanimous.
corrections_to_the_delivered_report.replacement: Any-hit retained as a descriptive statistic only, reported with its acceptance-set size, and never used to adjudicate a cross-tier comparison.

corrections_to_the_delivered_report.claim: the model's wall-confusion geometry is 'within 0.12 points' of the human value and its station geometry 'trails by 7.53 points'
corrections_to_the_delivered_report.evidence: Both shares are ratios over 65-72 wall errors and 64-69 station errors. Patient-clustered 95% CIs are [83.18, 96.00] for wall and [76.68, 93.36] for station. The station interval CONTAINS the human value 93.1, so the 7.5-point shortfall -- and the Phase 6 Grad-CAM lead built on it -- is not statistically supported.
corrections_to_the_delivered_report.replacement: Both comparisons reported as intervals. The wall result is stated as consistent with the human value; the station result is stated as underpowered, and the Phase 6 lead is downgraded from a finding to an untested hypothesis.

corrections_to_the_delivered_report.status: SCALE ARTEFACT (direction survives, magnitude does not)
corrections_to_the_delivered_report.evidence: The primary metric's attainable maximum falls with agreement (oracle marginalized macro F1: 100.00 / 74.23 / 44.55 / 40.23). Holding the ceiling constant, the S-unanimous - S-no-majority gap is 7.38 points, 95% CI [-3.08, +18.85] -- it does not exclude zero and does not exceed the 3.25 benchmark. The S-unanimous - S-majority (17.98, CI [12.49, 24.37]) and S-unanimous - S-plurality (25.21, CI [16.11, 34.11]) contrasts do both survive.
corrections_to_the_delivered_report.replacement: RQ1 is answered as supported for the 4/4 -> 3/4 and 4/4 -> 2-1-1 contrasts at 5.5-7.8x the architecture benchmark, and NOT supported for the 4/4 -> no-majority contrast the report led with. Raw and ceiling-normalised scales are both reported.
